mismatch.message: unsupported hero command: an unported branch of this command: applying a tool requires doapply()'s arm for object type 241

summary: The unmatched behavior is apply.c doapply() dispatch for FIGURINE (object type 241). In the assigned Wizard case, applying an uncursed gnome figurine to a valid adjacent floor square reaches use_figurine(), which asks for a direction and calls make_familiar(); the frozen JavaScript doapply() instead throws from its unported named-arm guard. The responsible apply.c source family is figurine_location_checks() and use_figurine(), with the FIGURINE dispatch wired in doapply(). Exact downstream parity also needs dog.c make_familiar() and its pick_familiar_pm() dependency: the C trace records make_familiar()'s rn2(10) result and creature outcome.

source.branch: A carried FIGURINE is selected by doapply(); the hero is not swallowed; getdir() selects an in-bounds adjacent floor square that is not obstructed or blocked by a boulder. The v14 input uses an uncursed gnome figurine and selects east.
callers: nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c: doapply() FIGURINE case calls use_figurine(&obj) and returns its ECMD result (lines 4367-4368); production JavaScript path is js/cmd.js runApplyCommand() -> js/apply.js doapply(). The frozen doapply() routes FIGURINE through DOAPPLY_UNPORTED_NAMED_ARMS and throws instead of reaching a handler (js/apply.js lines 3383-3394, 4447-4450).

nethack-c/upstream/src/cmd.c: command table maps the a/apply command to doapply() (line 1678); JavaScript mirrors this in js/extcmdlist_data.js and dispatches doapply through js/cmd.js (lines 3302-3307, 5148-5149).
dependencies: dog.c:make_familiar() is called by use_figurine() at apply.c:2574 and its return is discarded. The call still creates/configures the monster and consumes RNG; the v14 sourceTraceEvidence records rn2(10)=2 at dog.c:186. Leaving this call as note_unported preserves the explicit gap but cannot reproduce the recorded outcome.

dog.c:pick_familiar_pm() supplies a return value used by make_familiar(); for a FIGURINE it chooses mons[otmp->corpsenm] unless that monster is extinct. If make_familiar() is included, this helper must be included too.

apply.c:fig_transform() is the other source caller of dog.c:make_familiar() (apply.c:2424); it uses the returned monster. A whole make_familiar() port therefore has a second timed-transformation caller beyond the active apply path.

evidence: Saved diagnostic: .cache/synthetic-scans/v14/wizard-applies-uncursed-figurine.json stops after 41 emitted JavaScript screens at “applying a tool requires doapply()'s arm for object type 241”; challenges/evaluations/20260929225551-v14.json records 41/44 screens and 3 remaining screens. The manifest sourceTraceEvidence reports the next C RNG call as rn2(10)=2 at make_familiar(dog.c:186).

Source: nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:2510-2541 defines figurine_location_checks() for swallowed, bounds, obstruction and boulder checks; apply.c:2544-2581 defines use_figurine(), including its getdir() prompt, location check, transformation message, make_familiar() call, timer cancellation, object consumption, blind mapping, and ECMD_TIME result. apply.c:4367-4368 dispatches FIGURINE to use_figurine(&obj).

Frozen implementation: js/objects.js:316 defines FIGURINE as 241. At the examined commit, js/apply.js:3390 includes FIGURINE in DOAPPLY_UNPORTED_NAMED_ARMS and js/apply.js:4447-4450 throws for that set. The saved trace and evaluation identify the resulting stop; no assigned-session replay was needed.

Dependency trace: nethack-c/upstream/src/dog.c:138-215 contains make_familiar(); it uses pick_familiar_pm() at line 149, invokes makemon(), then for a figurine draws rn2(10) and chooses tame/peaceful/hostile effects. apply.c:2424 shows fig_transform() as its other caller.
